newsitem.title: USA: Fleet expects Middlesex County to default.
newsitem.headline: Fleet expects Middlesex County to default.

text.p: Fleet Financial Group said on Friday that it expected to be informed on Monday that Middlesex County, Massachusetts, located just west of Boston, had defaulted on $1.5 million of notes that the bank owns.
"We're waiting to be notified on Monday that the funds are not available from the paying agent. We're reserving the right to initiate legal remedies," said James Mahoney, a spokesman for Fleet.
The Fleet official said Boston Company owned the rest of the county's $4.5 million of revenue anticipation notes, but a spokesman from that firm was not available to comment.

The county's notes came due at 1630 EST, and the bank spokesman said state officials had told Fleet that Middlesex County, where Cambridge's Harvard University is located, had not met a 1500 EST deadline set by the state emergency board for providing a detailed financial plan.

The emergency board early this afternoon had turned down a request by the county to borrow approximately $6 million to repay the notes plus interest, saying that it wanted Middlesex to devise a long-term solution. The Weld Administration has proposed taking over the county governments, saying three to four have to be bailed out each year, and it could run them more efficiently.
Joe Landolfi, a spokesman for the state Executive Office for Administration and Finance, earlier said "This is the first time in memory that a default like this will have occurred."
